summary: Long text cut to its space — a line in a table cell, a paragraph under a heading — with the whole of it still reachable: a cut line is a tab stop with a tooltip on hover and focus, a cut paragraph has a Show more button. While the text fits it is plain text. The whole text is always in the DOM, so a screen reader reads all of it.
useWhen: text of any length lands in a space of fixed size — a description in a table row, a name in a card, a summary in a list
the text is written by users or agents, so no one can promise it is short

useInstead.when: the text is short by construction — a status, a label you wrote
useInstead.why: a label that is cut was written for a space it does not fit; shorten it instead

useInstead.when: an ID or key the user needs whole
useInstead.why: an ID is copied, not read; cutting it hides the part that tells two apart

useInstead.when: a long block of code or output
useInstead.why: it cuts by lines with Show more too, and keeps the code's spacing and a copy button

composition.note: `children` is the text, as a string. It takes the font of whatever it is in — put a caption class on it or on its parent. It never widens what it sits in: in a table cell, a grid or a flex row it shrinks to the space it is given and is cut there. `lines` above 1 clamps by line count; `overflow="expand"` swaps the tooltip for Show more, which a paragraph needs.

tooltip.use: the default — a short line in a narrow place: the cut line is a tab stop, and the tooltip shows the whole text on hover and focus

expand.use: a paragraph, with `lines` above 1 — Show more opens it in place, since a tooltip is too small to hold it

requires: plain text as `children` — nothing interactive inside a line that may be cut
guarantees: the whole text is in the DOM, cut by CSS: a screen reader reads all of it, find-in-page finds it, a copy copies it
a cut line is a tab stop, and focus opens the same tooltip as hover; Escape closes it
the tooltip is not the text's description — it repeats what is already read, so a screen reader does not hear it twice
Show more is a real button, with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the text
text that fits is plain text: no tab stop, no tooltip, no button; it measures again when its size changes
notes: a `title` attribute is hover-only and never reaches a keyboard — this replaces it
the focus ring is drawn inside the text's box, so a table's scroll container cannot clip it
it never widens its container: a table column, a grid track or a flex item shrinks to its share and cuts it

antiPatterns.why: a title appears on hover only, after a delay; a keyboard or touch user never gets the rest of the text
the rest is gone from the page: a screen reader, find-in-page and a copy all get the stub
a tooltip holds a sentence; a paragraph in one is unreadable and closes when the pointer leaves
